_comment: Merge the 'provider', 'model' and 'small_model' keys below into
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json on the CLIENT machine (OpenCode runs on the
workstation, not on the Spark). Replace the baseURL host with your Spark's
Tailscale IP or hostname.
limit.context is 114688 = the server's 131072 minus the 16384 output budget.
llama.cpp runs --parallel 1, so one slot holds prompt + generation, and
context shift is disabled by default: overflowing the window is a hard error
mid-run, not a silent truncation. Reserving the output keeps OpenCode
compacting before the server refuses.
The default model deliberately sets NO reasoning_effort. The GLM-5.3 chat
template honours only 'low' and 'high'; anything else — including the literal
string 'max' — falls through to 'max'. Omitting the key IS how you ask for
Max, which is what autonomous planning and tool selection need. Pinning it to
'low' globally starves exactly those turns.
glm-5.3-flash-low is the opt-in cheap lane for long straight code emission,
and is what small_model (titles, summaries) uses.
SAMPLING IS SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE — verified on the wire, not assumed.
OpenCode sends topP (camelCase). llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible API expects
top_p and IGNORES topP silently. Measured 2026-09-04: topP=0.001 at
temperature 2.0 produced 6 distinct outputs in 6 tries (no effect), while
top_p=0.001 produced 1 (collapsed to near-greedy, as expected).
So the topP value below is INERT. The effective top_p is whatever the server
was launched with (--top-p 0.95). It is kept here only so the intent is
visible and so it starts working if the client ever maps the field.
Change sampling in serving/glm53.env, not here.
What DOES reach the server: temperature (same spelling either way) and
chat_template_kwargs (snake_case, passed through untouched) — which is why
the reasoning_effort lane selection works.
